issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): the problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies messageOnMilk() returns a boolean (true if milking was successful, false otherwise) but the solution repository declares the interface and implementations with a String return type. Specifically: problem_statement.md (UML) defines messageOnMilk():boolean (lines 51-53) and the textual requirements state the method should return true/false (lines 92-95). In the solution, src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java declares 'String messageOnMilk();' (line 5) and concrete classes implement it as String: Goat.messageOnMilk() signature at src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java (line 15) and Seal.messageOnMilk() at src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java (line 19). This mismatch (boolean vs String) creates a clear contradiction that will confuse students about the required method signature and will cause tests or starter code expectations to fail depending on which variant is used.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the return type of Milkable.messageOnMilk() consistent across all artifacts. Choose one of the two options and apply consistently:

Option A (align statement to solution): Update the problem statement and UML to specify messageOnMilk() returns String and provide an example return value (e.g., "<AnimalType> <name> is milked"). Update any textual references that say boolean to match String.

Option B (align solution to statement): Change the interface and implementations to use boolean. Modify src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java to 'boolean messageOnMilk();' and update Goat.java and Seal.java to implement messageOnMilk() returning a boolean (true/false) and adjust any code or tests that rely on a String result (for example, change places that print the return value to instead print an explicit message when messageOnMilk() returns true). Also update the UML and problem text if needed to reflect the boolean behavior. Ensure tests and example Main code match the chosen signature.
